## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the pledge, the barring and what followed. None is used in this draft.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Hudaybiyyah, the treaty, and the names of those involved.
- 48:24 is not drafted because it names a town, and the town's name is listed as a name from later tradition in the shared fixtures of this repository; a scholar should decide whether the draft may name it.
- The Arabic word translated inviolable (a descriptive epithet of the mosque) is often rendered 'sacred'; a scholar should decide. The word translated 'vision' (ru'ya) can also be rendered 'dream'.
- The phrase translated 'the word of piety' (kalimat al-taqwa) is rendered closely; its meaning is left to commentary.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The pledge and the near victory  (`#the-pledge-and-the-near-victory`)

Cited ayat: 48:18-23

> **48:18** لَّقَدْ رَضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَٰبَهُمْ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا
>
> **48:19** وَمَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً يَأْخُذُونَهَا وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
>
> **48:20** وَعَدَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَهَا فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هَٰذِهِۦ وَكَفَّ أَيْدِىَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنكُمْ وَلِتَكُونَ ءَايَةً لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ صِرَٰطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا
>
> **48:21** وَأُخْرَىٰ لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا۟ عَلَيْهَا قَدْ أَحَاطَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرًا
>
> **48:22** وَلَوْ قَٰتَلَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوَلَّوُا۟ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا
>
> **48:23** سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ ٱللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا

### Claims

**c1** (48:18-19): God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the one addressed under the tree; He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity on them, rewarded them with a near victory and with abundant gains that they would take; God is Mighty, Wise.

**c2** (48:20-21): God had promised them abundant gains that they would take; He hastened this one for them and held back the hands of people from them, so that it would be a sign for the believers and guide them to a straight path; and there was another gain that they were not able to take, which God had encompassed; God has power over all things.

**c3** (48:22-23): Had those who disbelieved fought them, they would have turned their backs and then found no ally or helper; this is God's way that passed before, and no change will be found in God's way.

### One-minute summary

God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance under the tree, and He sent down tranquillity on them and rewarded them with a near victory [c1]. He held back the hands of people from them, and said that no change will be found in His way [c2][c3].

### Complete story

God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the one addressed under the tree [c1]. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity on them, rewarded them with a near victory and with abundant gains that they would take [c1].

God had promised them abundant gains that they would take; He hastened this one for them and held back the hands of people from them [c2]. This was so that it would be a sign for the believers and guide them to a straight path; and there was another gain that they were not able to take, which God had encompassed [c2].

Had those who disbelieved fought them, they would have turned their backs and then found no ally or helper [c3]. This is God's way that passed before, and no change will be found in God's way [c3].

### Deep study

The ayat link the pledge, God's knowledge of what was in the hearts, the tranquillity and the near victory in one sentence [c1]. They speak of gains in more than one way: gains that are taken now, and another gain they were not able to take, which God had encompassed [c2]. The statement about God's way is given as something that passed before and does not change [c3].

### Kids mode

The believers pledged allegiance under a tree, and God was pleased with them [c1]. God sent calm into their hearts and gave them a victory that was near [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tie God's pleasure to what He knew in their hearts [c1]. Another is that the ayat speak of God's way as one that does not change [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the tree was, when the pledge was given, or how many pledged; the ayat name neither the place nor the number.
- Not established: what the near victory was, or what the gains were; the ayat say only that they were near and abundant.
- Not established: who the people were whose hands were held back, or whether fighting had begun.
- Not established: whether these ayat describe a treaty; no treaty or its terms are mentioned in the verses cited.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Hudaybiyyah for the place, the treaty and its terms, and the number of those who pledged. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

## 2. Barred from the mosque  (`#barred-from-the-mosque`)

Cited ayat: 48:25-27

> **48:25** هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ وَٱلْهَدْىَ مَعْكُوفًا أَن يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُۥ وَلَوْلَا رِجَالٌ مُّؤْمِنُونَ وَنِسَآءٌ مُّؤْمِنَٰتٌ لَّمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ أَن تَطَـُٔوهُمْ فَتُصِيبَكُم مِّنْهُم مَّعَرَّةٌۢ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ لِّيُدْخِلَ ٱللَّهُ فِى رَحْمَتِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا۟ لَعَذَّبْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
>
> **48:26** إِذْ جَعَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ وَعَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ وَكَانُوٓا۟ أَحَقَّ بِهَا وَأَهْلَهَا وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمًا
>
> **48:27** لَّقَدْ صَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ ٱلرُّءْيَا بِٱلْحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ ٱلْحَرَامَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ءَامِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لَا تَخَافُونَ فَعَلِمَ مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا۟ فَجَعَلَ مِن دُونِ ذَٰلِكَ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا

### Claims

**c1** (48:25): They are those who disbelieved and barred the believers from the inviolable mosque and kept the offering from reaching its place; and had it not been for believing men and believing women whom the believers did not know, whom they might have trampled so that harm would have befallen them without knowing, God would have acted differently; this was so that God would admit into His mercy whom He wills; had they been distinct, God would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.

**c2** (48:26): When those who disbelieved set zeal in their hearts, the zeal of ignorance, God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers and made them keep to the word of piety, of which they were more worthy and more deserving.

**c3** (48:27): God made true the vision of His Messenger: you will enter the inviolable mosque, if God wills, in safety, with your heads shaved or cut short, not fearing; He knew what they did not know, and made, besides that, a near victory.

### One-minute summary

The ayat say that those who disbelieved barred the believers from the inviolable mosque, and that God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers [c1][c2]. They say that God made true the vision of His Messenger and made, besides that, a near victory [c3].

### Complete story

They are those who disbelieved and barred the believers from the inviolable mosque and kept the offering from reaching its place [c1]. Had it not been for believing men and believing women whom the believers did not know, whom they might have trampled so that harm would have befallen them without knowing, God would have acted differently [c1]. This was so that God would admit into His mercy whom He wills [c1].

When those who disbelieved set zeal in their hearts, the zeal of ignorance, God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers [c2]. He made them keep to the word of piety, of which they were more worthy and more deserving [c2].

God made true the vision of His Messenger: you will enter the inviolable mosque, if God wills, in safety, with your heads shaved or cut short, not fearing [c3]. He knew what they did not know, and made, besides that, a near victory [c3].

### Deep study

The ayat place a barrier and a reason for restraint side by side: those who barred the believers, and believers among them whom the believers did not know [c1]. The tranquillity is named for the Messenger and the believers together [c2]. The last ayah gives a vision made true, a promise of entering in safety, and a near victory made besides [c3].

### Kids mode

Some people kept the believers away from the mosque [c1]. God sent calm to His Messenger and the believers, and said that He made true the vision of His Messenger [c2][c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set the zeal of ignorance beside the tranquillity God sent down [c2]. Another is that the vision is joined to the words if God wills [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who barred them, where, when, or for how long; the ayat describe the barring and do not name the people or the place.
- Not established: what the offering was or how many were with it, or who the believing men and women they did not know were.
- Not established: when the vision was seen or what it showed beyond the entering and the shaved or shortened heads.
- Not established: whether the entering mentioned in the vision happened in the same year; the ayah says that God made, besides that, a near victory.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the place, the date and the sequence of events that these ayat are linked with.
